channel.description: Posts in the discussion thread "A Simple Bar" - serving drinks to all dimensions!

item.title: Re: A Simple Bar
item.content:encoded: Thank you for your take, you've given me a lot to think about. What I plan on is having most of the article being interviews with the bartender, what you suggested about the foundation not letting the bar sell anything and trying to anchor it and shut it down was an idea I had been thinking of in terms of ways to go with it for a while. For the whole emotional side of things, in the interviews i wanted to slowly make each interview feel more and more uneasy as the bartender finds he's not making any money and has to take more drastic measures. As to it not being an article and being a tale instead I feel as though it wouldn't work as well as a tale with it being mysterious happy to horror kind of story. I also have an ending that I've been planning since I first came up with the idea that really wouldn't work in a tale format. I hope I was able to clarify some things.

item.title: Re: A Simple Bar
item.content:encoded:
[+] Open for crit
– hide block

I'm not fully convinced by this as a SCP article: like, the actual emotional beats here and the story you're telling are pretty fun but it feels like having to tell this largely from the Foundation's perspective will feel weird and like, blunten the emotional impact.

Indeed, the Foundation's involvement here feels really awkward as a whole: if they know this place is anomalous, it really feels like they'd do more to keep it in containment than they do, and also that they wouldn't like…just let people go there as patrons? It also feels like a Foundation site is a strange place for a bar, like, I guess they function as small towns but it feels odd that the person thinks this is going to be the most effective place to put the bar and it feels odder that they turn out to be right?

I guess, when it comes down to it, what I am saying is that I think this would be best as a tale from the perspective of the bartender where the Foundation are at best minor side characters, or possibly a secondary antagonist. Like, if the story was the Foundation trying to shut down the bar, and the bartender trying to do everything in his power and being forced to keep moving the bar, then it feels like you'd have a lot more effective of a story; and it also feels like it'd help explain why e.g. the bartender isn't managing to make enough money. (I would still tell this as a tale from the perspective of the bartender if you want to do that though btw).

item.title: A Simple Bar
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Mystery/Horror

Page Layout (Optional): Interview logs and also a log about when the bar manifested and when the Foundation sent an MTF in to determine if the place is a threat

Elevator Pitch: A "simple" bar and owner of said bar, that has the ability to hop across dimensions in order to serve as many customers as possible. Said bar
sets up shop just outside a Foundation site in the middle of nowhere in the hopes of making more money.

Central Narrative:
+Block
-Block

The bartender and owner is relatively open and talkative about the people he's met and places he's been, but when the foundation start trying to find out
some of the more personal questions about his and the bars history he starts getting more dismissive and less talkative. My idea is that the Owner used to run the place with his brother until they traveled to a dimension they weren't welcome in, with the consequence being that the brother is kept half dead, bloody, and basically soulless chained up in the back room of the bar. The owner is unable to let his brother die and let himself move on, so he pays the strange man who lives in the dimension a fee every month for him to help keep his brother alive. In an attempt to make as much money as he can to pay the strangers increasing demands he puts his bar down next to a very busy Foundation site. The interviews with foundation staff start fine with the owner happily telling stories and chatting, but each interview he gets more and more reserved and disturbed with hints and clues as to his brothers fate, until just before an interview the owner comes out from the backroom with blood on his hands with tears in his eyes.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: What I'm trying to go for is it starting all happy with stories and fun banter and slowly see it turn into horror.

Additional Notes: I plan on leaving most of the history of the place only hinted at so the reader could speculate and come to their own conclusions.
